environmentalPersistence: Moderate — soil half-life ~7–100 days depending on conditions; detected in treated wastewater effluent and surface waters globally

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate — ibuprofen inhibits plant COX-like enzymes affecting growth signaling
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Moderate — root dysfunction impairs water uptake
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Mild to moderate — root tip necrosis at high doses
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Moderate — ibuprofen-induced anthocyanin response in Coleus reported in emerging literature
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Moderately to strongly inhibited — primary site of ibuprofen phytotoxicity
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Old leaves show chlorosis; root effects cause wilting across canopy

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Moderate — ibuprofen inhibits COX-like enzymes affecting lipid signaling and generates oxidative stress
molecularEffects.anthocyaninInduction: Moderate — one of the more interesting pharmaceutical effects on plant secondary metabolism

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Moderate — ibuprofen has antimicrobial properties at environmental concentrations
microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Moderately suppressed — PGPR including nitrogen-fixers sensitive to ibuprofen

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: 2–3 weeks — ibuprofen degrades in soil; partial recovery expected

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → mild purple tint (anthocyanin) + background chlorosis — distinctive pharmaceutical signature
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Root zone; then chlorosis spreading upward
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Root-to-shoot via water stress + systemic movement
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Purple tint + chlorosis combination — unusual and distinctive; different from pure signaling VOC pigmentation
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate purple-amber glow — anthocyanin + hydroxy-ibuprofen metabolite signature
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Moderate — new growth healthy after 2–3 weeks; original leaves partially recover

synergies.synergyNote: Pharmaceutical pollutant mixtures in wastewater effluent — ibuprofen, caffeine, and acetaminophen are the three most commonly co-detected pharmaceuticals in sewage-irrigated soils; combined microbiome disruption likely additive
synergies.antagonismNote: Ibuprofen inhibits COX-like enzymes involved in jasmonate synthesis — may partially antagonize MeJA-driven defense responses. Interesting crosstalk worth exploring.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Wastewater treatment plant effluent, hospital wastewater, sewage-irrigated agricultural fields, pharmaceutical manufacturing discharge — one of the most commonly detected pharmaceuticals in the environment globally
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Not intentionally applied — environmental contaminant from wastewater irrigation and sewage sludge application
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Low at therapeutic doses; ibuprofen toxicity at therapeutic doses is the concern for humans; environmental concentrations are far below therapeutic levels
educationalContext.climateLink: Climate-driven water scarcity is increasing use of treated wastewater for irrigation — increasing pharmaceutical exposure of agricultural soils globally
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Advil and Motrin — the most common painkiller in US homes — ends up in rivers and agricultural soil. Something every student has taken, now found in drinking water sources. Connects personal medicine use to environmental impact.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Pharmaceutical water pollution, emerging contaminants, wastewater irrigation, personal medicine and environment
